findings.reason: the section's contract is an enumeration of the behaviour changes and the test that pins them, so a node following it ships a silently widened input domain (a previously unreadable stamp now parsed) that no case in the deliverable names and no pinned case covers.
findings.text: §34 says `_created` going through `parse_utc` "changes two cases on purpose" (a zoneless string, and a whitespace-padded string that returns `None` today) and that "Any other unreadable string still returns None in both", but a lowercase `z` suffix is a third such case: measured with the repo's interpreter, `datetime.fromisoformat("2026-10-21T10:00:00z")` raises and `_created` returns `None` today, while `reckon/_timestamps.parse_iso` deliberately rewrites both `Z` and `z` to `+00:00` (`reckon/_timestamps.py:77`) so `parse_utc` reads it; the same widening applies to `_review_dispatch_instant`, whose "its results do not change" is justified only by the zoneless argument

findings.reason: the declared deliverable is half out of scope and half unmeasured, so the two deliberate result changes would land unpinned and the test that pins them is unwritable at the node's stated write scope.
findings.text: §34's Deliverable requires "A test pins both cases, the zoneless one under two `TZ` settings", but the Done-when measures only that the invariant test passes and that no test file importing either module adds a failure against a base arm, so a node that swaps the parser without pinning the two changed cases satisfies the gate; nor do the section's Write paths (`reckon/crew/model_catalogue.py`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py`) admit any test file, so a worker fenced to them cannot write the pinning test §33's sibling section does name ("Write paths: `tests/conftest.py` and the new test")
